newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal closes firm on China talk, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal closes firm on China talk, technicals.

text.p: Talk that China overnight bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal, along with commercial buying and a technical bounce, led CBOT soymeal futures to a higher close, traders said.
Soyoil also closed higher on a technical recovery, they said.
The market was hit Monday by talk that China cancelled purchases of soymeal, but early Tuesday there was talk that it entered the market overnight after recent falls in futures prices.
The commercial buying was significant, they said.

Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, bought 500 lots of December soymeal, Continental Grain bought 100 lots each of December and January, and Cargill Inc bought 400 lots of December, traders said. But Cargill also was a seller of 800 lots of March, they said.

The gains in soyoil were tied to technical signals. The nine day relative strength index for December soyoil closed at 30.242 points, near the 30 level which is an area many technicians consider moderately oversold.
Soyoil closed 0.03 to 0.14 cent per lb higher, with October up 0.13 at 22.75.
Soymeal closed $1.50 per ton higher to $1.50 lower, with October up $0.20 at $235.30.
The RSI for December soymeal closed at 21.335 points.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 27,589 Monday. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 24,000, down from 30,062 Monday.
